Path 2, sandboxGOALS §3.1

Kata Containers, gVisor, vCluster

Three ways to stop agent-written code sharing a kernel with everything else.

WHAT IT IS

Kata: each pod in a lightweight VM. gVisor: a user-space kernel intercepting syscalls. vCluster: a virtual Kubernetes control plane per agent or tenant inside a host cluster.

WHAT SETS IT APART

Kata gives the strongest isolation, and snapshots (Microsoft's 'Groundhog Pod') make start-up acceptable. gVisor is lighter with some compatibility cost. vCluster isolates the API surface, not the kernel.

WHERE WE STAND

A hardened pod now: non-root, read-only filesystem, no host mounts. Kata for any agent that executes generated code, from stage 3.

"Sandbox Your Agents" keynote; "Groundhog Pod" (Microsoft); vCluster, KubeCon NA 2026

TRIAL
